title: Sigil and Veil
premise: Coral Hartwell has spent nine years as the invisible keeper of the Gildergate, recording trades in impossible things—bottled griefs, borrowed years, names sold outright. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands and begs her to recover his daughter's soul from the court beneath Mount Vael, Coral realizes her own name appears in the guild's oldest ledger: she was traded once too. Descending with a disgraced sigil-smith and a veil that hides only what it chooses, she bargains, cheats, and finally burns her own ledger entry to buy the girl back before the last dragon-fire gutters out. In doing so she loses her invisibility forever—and gains, for the first time, a place she belongs.
about_author: Tamsin Fairweather is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's secrets before turning to fiction about the people who keep them. She writes in a drafty coastal cottage, accompanied by a one-eared cat named Ledger.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unwritten Names
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On a rain-lashed night at the Gildergate, a dying courier stumbles through the door Coral is sworn to keep shut, pressing a map into her hands and whispering a name that matches an entry in her oldest ledger. She refuses him—and he dies anyway, leaving her complicit. The emotional beat is guilt cracking open a carefully maintained invisibility; Coral realizes the guild has been trading in people like her all along.

chapters.title: What the Veil Chooses to Hide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Coral and Brannoc, a disgraced sigil-smith who owes the guild a debt of ink. They forge an uneasy alliance: he can rework the veil that lets them pass unseen beneath Mount Vael, but it demands a price paid in memory. Coral sacrifices her recollection of her mother's face. The beat is reluctant trust—the first belonging either has felt in years, purchased at real cost.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the dragon-fire-lit court below Vael, Coral discovers the soul they seek is bound beside hundreds of others—including, she learns, her own childhood self, sold by the family she barely remembers. Bargaining fails; the magistrate offers her freedom if she abandons the girl. The climax ignites as Coral burns her own ledger page in the guttering dragon-flame, unbinding every soul the fire holds, while Brannoc holds the collapsing gate open behind her.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing on Coral. Above ground, the freed souls scatter to whatever lives will take them back; the rescued girl, Wren, has no one waiting—except, unexpectedly, Coral. The guild marks Coral as traitor, ending her invisibility, but the gatekeepers' network quietly claims her as one of their own. The resolution lands on chosen belonging: Coral keeps a different gate now, one that opens, with Wren beside her and the map framed on the wall.
